purpose: Describe the verified procedural lifecycle after a citizen takes an approved next step, without promising processing time, acceptance or outcome.
core_principle: ACTION → SUBMITTED → RECEIVED → PROCESSED → OUTCOME/RECORD → REVIEW/APPEAL IF AVAILABLE → NEXT
rules: Describe only procedure stages supported by the governing source.
Submission does not equal acceptance, registration or favourable outcome.
Receipt does not equal substantive decision.
Processing stage does not establish the eventual outcome.
Do not invent processing times; distinguish statutory deadlines from indicative administrative timing.
If more information is requested, explain the purpose and route without assuming what the authority will decide.
Review and appeal routes are shown only where legally available.
Court or dispute routes are not presented as automatic escalation.
Enforcement is separate from decision-making and registration.
A procedural outcome does not automatically establish broader property rights outside its scope.
hard_stops: Never promise acceptance, registration, approval or a favourable outcome.
Never invent processing times or deadlines.
Never imply appeal rights without authority.
Never expose restricted evidence or internal reasoning.
